draft.briefing: Hey, you're in Kudremukh! The name means "horse-faced" in Kannada, after one side of the mountain that looks just like a horse's face.
draft.hungryLine: Kudremukh is a small hill and mining town, so eat at a local spot and save your energy for the views.

moodReplies.show-me-around: There's a temple about 10 minutes' walk away, and the Kudremukha peak itself is the big sight around here.
moodReplies.somewhere-to-chill: Just find a spot with a view of the mountain and try to spot the horse's face.
moodReplies.surprise-me: Kudremukha is Karnataka's second highest peak after Mullayanagiri, and the 26th highest in the Western Ghats.

spots.name: Temple
spots.detail: 10 min walk · A local place of worship

tips.title: Fly into Mangalore.
tips.body: The nearest international airport is at Mangalore, about 99 km away.

tips.title: Tread lightly in the park.
tips.body: Kudremukha National Park is a protected area of tropical wet evergreen forest, so leave nothing behind.

story.title: Samseparvata
story.body: The mountain was once called Samseparvata, because people approached it from Samse village.

story.title: An iron ore town
story.body: A small hill station and iron ore mining town grew up near the mountain, about 20 km from Kalasa.

story.title: A biodiversity hotspot
story.body: Kudremukha National Park covers 600.32 square km and is part of a UNESCO World Heritage Site, one of the world's 38 hottest hotspots of biodiversity.
